paragraphs: Rav Chisda’s student, as in Sukkah 29a; Hyman identifies him as Rami bar Chama.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital text of Sukkah 29a has bar Chama with the parenthesized form דרבה. The identification as Rami bar Chama is Hyman’s statement.

The saved Davidson Sukkah29a scalar has (דרבה) bar Chama in the Rav Chisda setting; the parentheses are digital wording, not inspected printed pixels. Rav Chisda’s student and the identification as Rami bar Chama remain Hyman’s statements. The witness does not by itself establish the Rabbah-to-Rami identification or an authority merge. Earlier wording about print refers only to the supplied digital text, without inspection of a printed page.
